government.note: Semi-presidential republic. The President is directly elected in a two-round vote for five years (at most two consecutive terms) and can dissolve the Assembly of the Republic and call early elections at their own discretion; six of the nine Assembly elections from 2000 to 2025 (2002, 2005, 2011, 2022, 2024, 2025) were early elections. The Prime Minister leads the government and needs the tolerance of the Assembly; day-to-day executive power lies with the government, so the Prime Minister is the effective executive.

holders.note: Elected in the second round on 8 February 2026; sworn in on 9 March 2026.

offices.note: Two-round direct election. The 2026 election was only the second to go to a second round, after 1986. Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa could not stand again in 2026 after two consecutive terms.

system.note: Closed-list proportional representation by the D'Hondt method in 22 multi-member constituencies (18 mainland districts, the Azores, Madeira, and two constituencies for voters abroad). No legal threshold. seats_2000 is the result of the 10 October 1999 election, with the CDU joint list split into its PCP (15) and PEV (2) members as recorded in the March 2000 budget vote.
